findings.title: Speech confidence is produced but no rule uses it
findings.problem: Stage 1 hands on a confidence value, but no rule in system_prompt.md says what the Router or Planner should do when confidence is low, so a misheard request can be searched as if it were certain.
findings.fix: Add a rule in the Pipeline or Enforced-by-code section: below a stated confidence, ask the shopper to repeat via the recording unclear reply, and do not search.

findings.title: No stated ranking criteria behind 'best fit first'
findings.problem: The table is labelled as ordered by 'best fit', but system_prompt.md never defines how fit is measured, which weakens the transparency obligation for a recommendation system under NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001.
findings.proof: the table is labelled as chosen and ordered by an AI assistant from its cited sources, best fit first
findings.fix: Add one sentence defining fit (for example, the shopper's stated constraints met first, then source-stated attributes) and require the Answerer to state it in the table note.

findings.title: No worked example of a product answer or abstention
findings.problem: The context specifies the table columns, spoken length and abstention form, but gives no example of a finished product answer or a not-found reply in knowledge_corpus or system_prompt, so output shape must be inferred.
findings.fix: Add one short example each for a product answer and a not-found reply in the knowledge corpus, kept brief.

findings.title: Tool-call budget is stated three different ways
findings.problem: The Planner is capped at three calls, the Retriever may add calls in two rounds, and the turn is capped at ten, so a reader cannot tell which limit binds.
findings.proof: a strategy and at most three tool calls with filters
findings.fix: State one total budget per turn and say how the Planner and Retriever share it.

findings.title: Router output field referenced but never defined
findings.problem: The fixed-sentence rules tell the Router to write a 'say' field, but no Router output schema exists in the supplied files, so the field's format and location are undefined.
findings.proof: the Router adds its id to "say"
findings.fix: Add the Router's output schema, including the 'say' field, to tool_schemas or the system prompt.

findings.title: Clarify-or-search rule is ambiguous
findings.problem: The Planner may ask one clarifying question when there is no product to search for, but the Router's rule to 'search when in doubt' conflicts with it, and the boundary is not stated.
findings.proof: or one clarifying question when there is no product to search for.
findings.fix: State the exact condition under which a clarifying question replaces a search.

findings.title: Loosening rules repeated between tool schema and system prompt
findings.problem: The rag.search description restates the never-loosened list and loosening order, which the system prompt already summarises, so the same policy is paid for twice in every call context.
findings.proof: Never loosened: safety exclusions, a stated age range, a price floor, and the under-three rule
findings.fix: Keep the full loosening order in the tool description only and cut the system prompt's restatement to a one-line pointer.

findings.title: Pipeline narrative duplicates the Enforced-by-code section
findings.problem: The nine-stage pipeline restates input screen, search, grounding and rule-check behaviour that the Enforced-by-code and Safety sections repeat in full, adding a large block of redundant text.
findings.proof: Input screen (code) -> the message without declined clauses and with personal details replaced.
findings.fix: Keep the pipeline as a short stage list with one line per stage and move behavioural detail to the enforced section only.

findings.title: Catalog facts repeated across three files
findings.problem: The January 2020 snapshot, the 9,740-product count and the no-ratings fact appear in the tool schema, the system prompt and catalog_and_sources.md, with no reader gain from the repetition.
findings.proof: Catalog prices are from a January 2020 snapshot.
findings.fix: State each catalog fact once, in the knowledge file, and reference it from the other two.

findings.title: Instruction-stripping relies on an unspecified server step
findings.problem: The context depends on the MCP server to remove instruction-like text, but no detail is given on how it is detected or what happens when it misses, so a model can still receive injected text.
findings.proof: The MCP server removes instruction-like text from tool results (catalog listings and web results) before any model sees it
findings.fix: Document the server's detection method and add a model-side rule that treats any remaining instruction-like text as data and reports it.

findings.title: No guidance on the top_k or price_max defaults
findings.problem: rag.search gives top_k a default of 5 but no guidance on when to change it, and web.search's price_max is described without saying what happens when results carry no price.
findings.fix: Add one clause to top_k on when to use fewer or more results and one to price_max on how unpriced results are handled.

context_engineering.summary: The context is clearly scoped and well fenced against injection, but it repeats its policies across the system prompt, tool descriptions and knowledge files, leaves speech confidence and ranking criteria unused or undefined, and has a few precedence and budget ambiguities to close.
